evidence.claim: For 2022, Brazil's inflation target was 3.5% with a 1.5-point tolerance band, but actual inflation was 5.79%, triggering an open letter on the breach.
evidence.title: Our Results
evidence.excerpt: For 2022, Brazil's inflation target was 3.5% with a 1.5-point tolerance band, but actual inflation was 5.79%, triggering an open letter on the breach.
evidence.source_locator: Annual report section on inflation and purchasing power
evidence.source_confidence_reason: The central bank is the authoritative source for the target framework and annual inflation breach.
evidence.period_fit: Directly about 2022 and published as the annual report for that year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Contextual and partly attributable to the administration's policy environment; the BCB itself is institutionally independent.
contrary_evidence: The inflation-targeting framework itself was inherited and independent of Bolsonaro.
This does not prove presidential mismanagement on its own.

evidence.claim: Copom said Brazilian activity was growing above expectations and the labor market was recovering, but inflation remained high and broad-based, with food and fuel shocks still prominent.
evidence.title: Atas do Comitê de Política Monetária - Copom
evidence.excerpt: Copom said Brazilian activity was growing above expectations and the labor market was recovering, but inflation remained high and broad-based, with food and fuel shocks still prominent.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary central-bank minutes documenting the state of the 2022 economy and inflation drivers.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Contextual rather than directly attributable to Bolsonaro, but relevant to the administration's economic environment and response choices.
contrary_evidence: The central bank attributes some weakness to global and commodity shocks.
Positive output and labor recovery complicate any one-direction verdict.

evidence.claim: Congress approved a spending package Bolsonaro was banking on for reelection that bypassed the spending cap and boosted social benefits, prompting investor concern about fiscal discipline and inflation.
evidence.title: Brazil Congress approves major spending bill, lifting Bolsonaro re-election hopes
evidence.excerpt: Congress approved a spending package Bolsonaro was banking on for reelection that bypassed the spending cap and boosted social benefits, prompting investor concern about fiscal discipline and inflation.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting is strong independent coverage, though the piece relies partly on market expectations and political context.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct enough to Bolsonaro's reelection strategy because the package was explicitly tied to his campaign and administration.
contrary_evidence: Government said it needed urgent relief for households hit by inflation.
The package had congressional approval, not sole presidential unilateral action.

evidence.claim: Reuters estimated that Bolsonaro's 2022 election-year benefits and promises would cost R$273 billion in 2022-2023, with R$127.4 billion already approved and implemented.
evidence.title: SAIBA MAIS-Benefícios em série e promessas de Bolsonaro em ano eleitoral têm custo de R$273 bi em 2022 e 2023
evidence.excerpt: Reuters estimated that Bolsonaro's 2022 election-year benefits and promises would cost R$273 billion in 2022-2023, with R$127.4 billion already approved and implemented.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters is a strong independent source, and the UOL mirror preserves the original report and numbers.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022 and tied to the election period.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Bolsonaro's election strategy and executive choices.
contrary_evidence: Some measures were already approved through Congress, not by executive fiat alone.
Short-term relief can be justified in inflationary periods, but fiscal sustainability is the counterpoint.

evidence.claim: Bolsonaro issued a decree delegating to the Economy Minister authority over opening 2022 budget credits and related budget adjustments to speed execution.
evidence.title: Decreto prevê delegação de competências ao Ministro de Estado da Economia
evidence.publisher: Secretaria-Geral da Presidência / Governo do Brasil
evidence.excerpt: Bolsonaro issued a decree delegating to the Economy Minister authority over opening 2022 budget credits and related budget adjustments to speed execution.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: This is the official government announcement of an enacted decree with a clear administrative delegation.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct and strong: this was a presidential decree under Bolsonaro's authority.
contrary_evidence: Delegation does not prove the minister was competent, only that he was empowered.
Budget execution still faced fiscal and inflationary constraints.

evidence.claim: The PPI said it concluded 48 projects in 2022 and secured more than R$101 billion in contracted investments, including the Eletrobras capitalisation and airport concessions.
evidence.title: Secretaria Especial do PPI concluiu 48 projetos em 2022 e assegurou R$ 101 bilhões em novos investimentos
evidence.excerpt: The PPI said it concluded 48 projects in 2022 and secured more than R$101 billion in contracted investments, including the Eletrobras capitalisation and airport concessions.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official year-end program report on completed projects and contracted investment, with clear implementation language.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to the Bolsonaro administration's investment-policy execution, though project-level economics depend on private actors and regulators.
contrary_evidence: Contracted investments are not the same as realized household welfare gains.
Infrastructure gains are long run and uneven.

evidence.claim: The government said Plano Safra 2022/23 would provide R$340.88 billion in rural credit, up 36% from the previous plan.
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock / Government of Brazil
evidence.excerpt: The government said Plano Safra 2022/23 would provide R$340.88 billion in rural credit, up 36% from the previous plan.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: This is the official launch page for the 2022/23 rural credit program, with the stated amount and percentage increase.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct government policy under Bolsonaro, though sectoral benefits are concentrated in agriculture rather than the whole economy.
contrary_evidence: Sectoral credit expansion can help productivity but does not prove broad household welfare gains.
Agricultural output can also be exposed to commodity and weather cycles.

evidence.claim: The federal government reported a 2022 primary surplus of R$59.7 billion, above the year's formal projection.
evidence.title: Governo Federal apresenta superávit primário de R$ 59,7 bilhões em 2022
evidence.excerpt: The federal government reported a 2022 primary surplus of R$59.7 billion, above the year's formal projection.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: National Treasury is the authoritative source for the official fiscal outcome and the release gives the final figure directly.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partly attributable to the Bolsonaro administration's fiscal choices, but the result also reflects one-offs, transfers, and revenue conditions beyond his control.
contrary_evidence: A surplus does not erase election-year spending expansion or inflation pressure.
The headline result may not reflect underlying sustainability or quality of spending.

evidence.claim: The government said about 500,000 poor or extremely poor families were added to Auxílio Brasil in October 2022, bringing coverage to 21.1 million families and guaranteeing a minimum payment of R$600 per family.
evidence.title: Quase 500 mil famílias passam a integrar o programa Auxílio Brasil em outubro
evidence.excerpt: The government said about 500,000 poor or extremely poor families were added to Auxílio Brasil in October 2022, bringing coverage to 21.1 million families and guaranteeing a minimum payment of R$600 per family.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official program announcement with a clear beneficiary count and benefit floor.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to the Bolsonaro administration's cash-transfer policy and election-year execution, though some components were congressional or constitutional in origin.
contrary_evidence: The announcement is a policy claim, not an independent outcome evaluation.
The expansion also had an obvious election-year political dimension.

evidence.claim: Bolsonaro signed a law creating Internet Brasil, a program to provide free mobile broadband to public-school students from CadÚnico families.
evidence.title: Governo Federal garante acesso à internet para alunos da rede pública
evidence.excerpt: Bolsonaro signed a law creating Internet Brasil, a program to provide free mobile broadband to public-school students from CadÚnico families.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official announcement of a signed law and the stated target population.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct presidential action, although implementation was shared with the communications and education ministries.
contrary_evidence: The page is promotional and does not measure take-up or learning gains.
Program creation is not the same as durable delivery.

evidence.claim: Anatel approved a pilot to bring broadband internet to 177 public basic-education schools by March 2023 as part of a R$3.1 billion school-connectivity commitment.
evidence.title: Conselho Diretor aprova piloto para conectividade nas escolas
evidence.excerpt: Anatel approved a pilot to bring broadband internet to 177 public basic-education schools by March 2023 as part of a R$3.1 billion school-connectivity commitment.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official regulator announcement with a concrete implementation milestone, though the commitment sits partly outside direct executive control.
evidence.period_fit: Late 2022 implementation context, with delivery extending into early 2023.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partly attributable to Bolsonaro-era policy design, but implementation was shared with regulators and telecom operators.
contrary_evidence: This is a pilot, not a full-system roll-out.
The funding came from telecom obligations, not only presidential spending choices.

evidence.claim: Bolsonaro's 2022 plan centered on freedom, economic liberalism, privatization, tax simplification, job creation, and keeping Auxílio Brasil at R$600, while seeking OECD entry.
evidence.title: Conheça os planos de governo dos candidatos à Presidência
evidence.excerpt: Bolsonaro's 2022 plan centered on freedom, economic liberalism, privatization, tax simplification, job creation, and keeping Auxílio Brasil at R$600, while seeking OECD entry.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Secondary source, but it directly summarizes the TSE-filed campaign plan and lists the core economic priorities.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable as Bolsonaro's filed 2022 campaign program; it reflects stated priorities, not execution.
contrary_evidence: This is campaign rhetoric, so it shows intent more than implementation.

evidence.claim: The new voluntary civil service program combined qualification courses for unemployed workers with public-interest activities in participating municipalities.
evidence.title: Presidente Bolsonaro cria o Programa Nacional de Serviço Civil Voluntário
evidence.excerpt: The new voluntary civil service program combined qualification courses for unemployed workers with public-interest activities in participating municipalities.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official launch notice with a clear description of the program's design and target group.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable: Bolsonaro signed the measure and it was presented as his government's program, though rollout and results are not shown here.
contrary_evidence: This is a program announcement; execution scale and outcomes are not shown in the source.

evidence.claim: The program aimed to eradicate child labor and slavery-like labor, combat discrimination, and promote formalization of employment.
evidence.title: Governo Federal lança programa para promover o trabalho responsável e decente
evidence.excerpt: The program aimed to eradicate child labor and slavery-like labor, combat discrimination, and promote formalization of employment.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official announcement states concrete labor-market objectives and implementation intent.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Bolsonaro's government through the labor ministry; the source shows declared action, not measured success.
contrary_evidence: The announcement is a launch, not an outcome study; execution remains to be checked.

evidence.claim: The government cut import tariffs by another 10% on 6,195 tariff codes, presenting the change as a way to lower prices and support trade and production.
evidence.title: Governo Federal anuncia nova redução de 10% no Imposto de Importação de bens comercializados
evidence.excerpt: The government cut import tariffs by another 10% on 6,195 tariff codes, presenting the change as a way to lower prices and support trade and production.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official ministry release with precise tariff counts, purpose, and policy scope.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Bolsonaro's government and economic team; it is a concrete policy choice even if downstream effects were broader than the presidency alone.
contrary_evidence: The release presents long-run gains; actual pass-through and distributional effects were uncertain.

evidence.claim: The December 2022 agreement kept fuels and electricity essential for ICMS and was presented as a structural measure to lower consumer prices while preserving fiscal security.
evidence.title: União, Estados e Distrito Federal assinam acordo que visa manter a redução do preço dos combustíveis e da energia elétrica
evidence.excerpt: The December 2022 agreement kept fuels and electricity essential for ICMS and was presented as a structural measure to lower consumer prices while preserving fiscal security.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official ministry account of a signed agreement tied to specific tax treatment and price objectives.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Bolsonaro's government and federal-state negotiation, though price effects were mediated by states, courts, and markets.
contrary_evidence: The source is official self-description; later price effects may depend on state implementation and market pass-through.

evidence.claim: Congress approved a Bolsonaro-backed spending package that bypassed the spending cap to raise social benefits, with investors warning about fiscal discipline and inflation.
evidence.title: Brazil Congress approves major spending bill, lifting Bolsonaro re-election hopes
evidence.excerpt: Congress approved a Bolsonaro-backed spending package that bypassed the spending cap to raise social benefits, with investors warning about fiscal discipline and inflation.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters reporting on a major legislative action and market reaction.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable as Bolsonaro's political strategy and government-backed push, but final enactment depended on Congress.
contrary_evidence: The government's justification was that the measures were urgent relief for people hurt by high inflation.

evidence.claim: IBGE reported that average real household income per capita rose 6.9% in 2022 and said labor-market recovery and Auxílio Brasil helped income recovery.
evidence.title: In 2022, labor market and Auxílio Brasil cash transfer program allow income recovery
evidence.excerpt: IBGE reported that average real household income per capita rose 6.9% in 2022 and said labor-market recovery and Auxílio Brasil helped income recovery.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official statistics agency retrospective using survey data with a direct 2022 period fit.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attribution is mixed: the data capture outcomes during Bolsonaro's final year, but IBGE explicitly links the gain to labor-market recovery and Auxílio Brasil rather than Bolsonaro alone.
contrary_evidence: The same article says income from all jobs fell 2.1%, so the improvement was mixed and partly transfer-driven.

The original TSE-filed 2022 program is only indirectly represented here through a secondary summary.
Independent outcome audits for several flagship measures are still thinner than the implementation claims.
